decisions_log.question: Java bare-vs-qualified method identity after the duplicate-traversal fix
decisions_log.decision: QUALIFIED ONLY. Java keeps `Outer.alpha` as type `method`; the bare `alpha` function element is DROPPED, not shimmed.
decisions_log.rationale: A nested-construct probe against HEAD showed the double-walk causes THREE defects from ONE root cause, not the one the ticket described: (i) exact duplicates, multiplicative with nesting depth - a C++ method at depth 2 emitted x4; (ii) MIS-SCOPED names - a nested type's members attributed to the OUTER type (`Outer.beta` for a method on `Inner`, `Outer.gamma` for a method on `Contract`), which are false facts rather than inflated counts; (iii) the bare/qualified fork. Because all three share the root cause they are not separable: any fix that removes the duplicates also removes the bare names, so preserving them would mean deliberately RE-EMITTING them as a shim - strictly more work than (A), built in phase 1 and deleted in phase 2 by this same program, since phase 2 (TKT-XGZA82) IS the bare-name reduction at tree-sitter-file-scan.ts:63. Nothing in CODEREF-CORE itself consumes Java/C++/Rust elements (this repo is TypeScript), so exposure is downstream repos scanning those languages across a one-phase window.
rejected_alternatives: B - bare only: Java would stop producing methods and diverge from every other language.
C - keep both via a compatibility shim: considered and rejected as more work than A, with the shim scheduled for deletion in the very next phase.

decisions_log.summary: Exactly three double-visit sites; the canonical fix already exists twice in this same file.
broken_sites: element-extractor.ts:480-483 Rust impl_item - scoped traverse then falls through to the unconditional child loop.
already_correct: element-extractor.ts:346 Python class_definition carries `return; // Don't double-traverse class children` - this IS the fix shape.
element-extractor.ts:141 + :206 TypeScript function_declaration and class_declaration carry the same guard (the prior recursion-leak fix).
Go (extractGoElements) has no scoped sub-traverse at all - unaffected.
decisions_log.additional_defect_found: Java interface_declaration (:564-575) never traverses its body scoped AND never returns, so interface members are attributed to the ENCLOSING class (`Outer.gamma`). Fixing the class branch alone would NOT fix this; the interface branch needs its own scoped traverse + return to make the member `Contract.gamma`.
decisions_log.dead_code_confirmed: Rust `parentScope`/`implType` is threaded but never read (lines 451-507), and the C++ branch never reads `parentScope` either. Neither language has qualification to preserve, so both are dedup-only under ruling A; introducing scoped names there would be NEW behavior and is OUT of scope for this phase.

SAFE - zero .name/.calls/.imports references; it hands the array to writeIndexVariants and saveRoutesToFile.
SAFE - reads `func.calls?.length` only. Counts, never matches.

LOAD-BEARING BOTH WAYS. :96 builds `element:{file}:{name}`, so two same-named methods in one file COLLIDE into a single node id - already broken by the bare form today. :125 then resolves call targets by BARE callee name within the file. Qualifying element.name would fix the collision and simultaneously break :125.

NOT IN THE PLAN'S LIST. Indexes elementMap BY BARE NAME and warns "Function X is called but not found in codebase" when a callee misses. Under option (B) every method would be indexed as `Outer.alpha` while callees stay bare `alpha`, turning EVERY method call into a false undefined-call warning. This is the finding that decides the ruling.

NOT IN THE PLAN'S LIST. Keys `${file}:${name}`, so same-named methods merge into one diagram node AND their callee sets union - the same symptom as the extractor defect, manifesting in a second place.

decisions_log.decisive_asymmetry: CALLEES must stay BARE - all three name-keyed consumers resolve a callee by its bare name, and cross-file resolution has nothing else to key on. ELEMENT IDENTITY must become unique - the same three consumers collide on it today. Those pull in opposite directions, which is why "just qualify everything" (option B) is not merely larger, it is WRONG: it would break validateReferences outright.

decisions_log.root_cause: import-resolver.ts:301-306 dropped RawExportFact.localName when building the reExport ExportTableEntry, so resolveTransitiveReExport:413 recursed into the upstream module asking for the DOWNSTREAM alias. The extractor was never at fault - relationship-extractor.ts:745-748 splits nameNode from aliasNode correctly. The fact arrived well-formed and the table kept half of it. Same class as phase 1 and phase 2: two components disagree about a name and nothing tested the seam.
decisions_log.fix: ExportTableEntry gains optional localName; the reexport/namespace branch carries fact.localName through; resolveTransitiveReExport recurses with `direct.localName ?? exportedName`. The wildcard branch is deliberately left alone - `export * from` cannot rename, so it must keep asking for the requested name. +30/-1 in one file.
decisions_log.ac1_proof: RAN, not asserted. Reverted src/pipeline/import-resolver.ts to HEAD and re-ran the file: cases (a)(b)(c)(e) FAIL, and all four guards - un-renamed re-export, wildcard, a->b->a cycle, and the genuinely-missing-upstream case (d) - PASS. Restored after.

p3_t6_real_repo_measure.method: Full PipelineOrchestrator run over coderef-core, before and after, comparing importResolutions.
p3_t6_real_repo_measure.why_zero_and_why_it_is_not_a_null_result: All six renamed re-exports in this repo are `export { default as X }` inside a sub-barrel, and NO internal file imports through them. They are reached only from src/index.ts via `export * from ./analyzer/index.js` and friends - the PACKAGE PUBLIC SURFACE. So the broken consumer was never inside this repo; it was anyone writing `import { GraphExporter } from "@coderef/core"`. That path is wildcard-then-rename, two branches composing, and it was broken at HEAD. Verified as test case (e), which fails at HEAD and passes after - it is NOT implied by (a)-(d) precisely because the wildcard branch is intentionally not localName-aware. Reporting the zero plainly: on THIS repo the fix is prophylactic, same posture as the dist-*/ rule in TKT-HZF70M. The fixture proof is the evidence, not the repo delta.
